uploaded_reference.title: NCCN Guidelines for Patients: Neuroendocrine Tumors
uploaded_reference.based_on: NCCN Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors Version 1.2026 — April 21, 2026

mapping.decision: Original definitions and shared decision prompts; no copied illustrations.

mapping.concepts: History, safety bloods, biomarkers, CT/MRI, receptor and FDG imaging, inherited risk
mapping.decision: Distinguishes diagnostic/response/hormone questions from regimen safety tests. Echo described for cardiac/valve assessment, not as a diagnostic test for the syndrome itself.

mapping.concepts: Resectability, hormone function, primary site, stage, grade and differentiation
mapping.decision: Stage and grade are explicitly separate. SSTR expression does not itself imply a functioning tumour. No numeric Ki-67 grade threshold imported.
General context only. US preferred therapy lists, access and reimbursement not transferred to NCCP eligibility. Existing SACTCheck anatomy retained.

mapping.concepts: Trials, supportive care, decisions and follow-up
mapping.decision: Original plain-language explanation of uncertainty, quality of life and care coordination; no US payment assumptions.

mapping.concepts: GI NET context and carcinoid symptoms
mapping.decision: Hormone symptoms and need for a personalised plan used. Surgical surveillance intervals not imposed on active SACT; no expansion to functional GI everolimus.
Reviewed to avoid importing lung indications into the four Irish catalogue regimens; not presented as a new lung suite.

mapping.concepts: Pancreatic NET distinction, hormone syndromes and treatment planning
mapping.decision: Pancreatic NET kept distinct from pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Pancreatic hormone examples remain conditional; no generic biochemical surveillance mandate.
Used to explain distinctions from grade 1/2 and NEC. Does not expand Irish PRRT or GI-everolimus eligibility to grade 3.

mapping.authored_locations: net-diagnosis; net-tests; passport pathology and family-history discussion
mapping.decision: Different diagnoses remain distinct. Genetic counselling is conditional; no assumption that all NETs are inherited.
Original prompts for local transport, work, care, financial and emotional support. No US helpline, funding or service availability promises.
Consulted terminology; no glossary text copied. Avoided equating receptor expression with excess hormone release.

source_hierarchy: Current NCCP regimen: Irish clinical indication, schedule and primary dose/monitoring rules.
Current EMA product information: explicit supplementary medicine safety, with differences retained for specialist review.
Current HSE PRRT patient leaflets: Irish service arrangements and individual radiation-safety workflow; deviations from current NCCP/EMA not silently merged.
User-supplied NCCN patient guide: education structure and discussion concepts only.
Primary trial reports: population-specific evidence, limitations and endpoints; no invented personal percentages.
NCI PDQ: supplementary marker, hormone and digestive background only.
gaps_and_deliberate_limits: No source supplies one mandatory CT/MRI, PET, chromogranin A, 5-HIAA or hormone schedule for all four regimens. Patient plans ask the consultant to specify purpose and timing.
The guide includes lung, grade 3 and NEC options not included in these exact Irish catalogue entries. They are not presented as authorised extensions.
General patient guidance does not settle dose-table conflicts, recurrence histories or combined organ/toxicity reductions; audit agents and clinician review handle those.
Irish PRRT and EMA general radiation restrictions differ; the individual medical-physicist written card and instructions control patient practice.
The full supplied PDF and NCCN art are not redistributed inside the application. New prose is original and existing anatomical art is preserved.
No NCCN endorsement, completed independent clinical/pharmacy/PPI approval, live deployment or real-device validation is claimed.
clinical_review_status: Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
